title: The Khalsa Consolidates Its Hold on Doaba

blocks.text: With Bishambhar defeated, the poem shifts from battlefield action to the political work of settlement. After collective resolve and prayer, the Singhs spread out to occupied villages in the Doaba region, turning a single victory into a broader pattern of local control.

Possession is shown taking several forms at once: some settlements invite Sikh protection, some are retained through old relationships, and others are held because no one can dislodge the first claimant. Where rival claims arise, misl authority begins to matter more than raw momentum, because disputes must now be judged rather than merely fought.

The page therefore explains how plunder matures into governance. Revenue, recognized possession, and expanding contingents show the Buddha Dal becoming not just a raiding force but a power able to stabilize and enlarge its own territorial order.
